searches.title: Sport Coats & Blazers
searches.benchmark: Major priority. Visual benchmark: the J. Press Light Olive Barleycorn Harris Tweed Sport Coat — muted, sophisticated, earthy brown/olive/taupe, traditional Ivy/English-country feel.
searches.criteria: Major priority category. Harris Tweed, Donegal, Shetland and other high-quality English/Scottish wool. Prioritize herringbone, barleycorn, subtle nailhead, gun club and restrained checks. Colors: peat brown, brown-grey, taupe, lovat, olive-brown, tobacco, oatmeal, charcoal, moss, muted rust, and earthy color-blends that read as a sophisticated muted brown from a distance. Favor soft/natural shoulders, 3-roll-2 sack construction, traditional two/three-button jackets and classic proportions — a sport coat/blazer, not an overcoat. Strongly prefer jackets with brown leather (or leather-look) buttons over horn, corozo or plastic buttons — leather buttons are a strong positive signal here and should be called out explicitly in matchNote whenever visible in listing photos or description. Brands: J. Press, Brooks Brothers, Ralph Lauren / Polo Ralph Lauren / Purple Label, Dunn & Co., O'Connell's, The Andover Shop, Southwick, Norman Hilton, Chipp, Paul Stuart, quality Harris Tweed makers, Magee, DAKS, Austin Reed, Burberry/Burberrys, Aquascutum, and other excellent vintage British, Scottish, Irish or American tailoring. Avoid orange/rust-dominant tweeds and loud plaids. Condition: good wearable vintage or better — avoid significant moth damage, holes, permanent stains or structural damage. Price: prioritize under $300, ideally under $200; an exceptional piece can run higher.

searches.title: Suits
searches.benchmark: Timeless natural-shoulder suiting — Brooks Brothers Golden Fleece or vintage Savile Row flannel as the touchstone, not a corporate business suit.
searches.criteria: Timeless suits rather than corporate business suits: charcoal flannel, medium grey flannel, subtle chalk stripe, navy, brown, olive and understated Prince of Wales checks. Favor natural shoulders, higher-rise trousers, classic lapels and traditional proportions; two-piece and three-piece both welcome. Brands: Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Polo Ralph Lauren, Brooks Brothers Golden Fleece, J. Press, Paul Stuart, O'Connell's, Hickey Freeman, Southwick, vintage Savile Row (Anderson & Sheppard, Huntsman, Kilgour, Henry Poole, Chester Barrie), Canali, Corneliani, Caruso, Ring Jacket and other excellent traditional tailoring. Sizing: jacket 36S–38S preferred (also 36R/38R/40S or untagged vintage if measurements suggest tailoring potential); trousers 30–33in waist, 30–32in inseam, higher rise. Condition: good wearable vintage or better.

styleGuide:
WARDROBE MISSION: help build a cohesive wardrobe in the English Ralph Lauren / Ivy League / country-house aesthetic across categories — sophisticated, masculine, textured, slightly lived-in, timeless, luxurious without being flashy. Think Ralph Lauren Purple Label and vintage Polo mixed with J. Press, old Brooks Brothers, Drake's, Savile Row, Harris Tweed, English country clothing and classic American Ivy.

AVOID: generic 'old money' aesthetic, trendy Instagram/preppy clothing, skinny modern tailoring, conspicuous designer logos, flashy luxury, overly precious formalwear, costume-like British country clothing, and cheap modern approximations when authentic vintage or heritage pieces are available.

SIZING (approx. 5'7"): trousers 30–33in waist, 30–32in inseam; shirts Small or Medium; sweaters Small or Medium; sport coats/suits 36S–38S preferred; shoes/loafers US 9.5. For vintage tailoring, don't rely only on tagged size — include 36R, 38R, 40S or untagged jackets when measurements suggest they could work with reasonable tailoring. Jacket ideal range: ~17–18in shoulders, ~19–21in pit-to-pit, ~28–29.5in back length; sleeves and waist are easily altered. Prioritize correct shoulders and overall proportions over the tag.

HOW TO SHOP: search eBay, Grailed, Etsy, Poshmark, Depop, Mercari, The RealReal, Vestiaire Collective, consignment shops, specialist vintage menswear dealers, independent vintage stores and heritage retailers. Don't just search brand names — combine fabric + color + garment + size + heritage terms so obscure, unbranded, poorly-titled or undervalued high-quality vintage pieces surface too. Prioritize vintage/secondhand where quality clearly exceeds price; don't reject something purely for tagged size when tailoring could make it work.

QUALITY BAR & REPORTING: each morning, focus primarily on newly listed items and exceptional older listings not shown before. Report ONLY genuinely good finds — 5–15 per category is plenty; never pad with mediocre or loosely-related results just to hit a number. For each: brand, tagged size, actual measurements (if available), fabric, color/pattern, condition, price, seller/platform, direct link — plus a short note on why it fits the wardrobe and any sizing/tailoring caveats. The goal is not to accumulate clothes; the goal is a cohesive, high-quality wardrobe where almost everything works together.
